header.one_liner: Drishti is GalaxEye's Earth-observation satellite carrying the world's first OptoSAR payload — fusing optical and synthetic-aperture-radar imaging on one platform.
header.indigenous_label: India-developed (IIT Madras origin); no audited indigenous percentage disclosed

at_a_glance.Claim: World's first OptoSAR satellite; among India's largest privately built satellites
at_a_glance.Significance: Dual-sensor imaging able to see through cloud/weather and in daylight

what_it_is.prose: Drishti is the maiden commercial Earth-observation satellite of GalaxEye, a Bengaluru-based deep-tech company that traces its origins to a student team at IIT Madras. Its headline technology is 'OptoSAR' — a payload that fuses optical imagery with synthetic-aperture radar (SAR) on a single satellite, combining SAR's all-weather, day-and-night, cloud-penetrating capability with the interpretability of optical images. GalaxEye describes Drishti as the world's first OptoSAR satellite and among the largest privately built satellites from India, launched on a SpaceX rideshare mission in 2026 under 'Mission Drishti'. The fused dataset targets applications such as agriculture, disaster response, infrastructure and defence-relevant monitoring where persistent, weather-independent imaging matters. This is an honest Tier B entry: the launch and world-first framing are well covered in credible press and the company's own material, but detailed on-orbit performance figures and the customer/order book remain thin, so specific resolution and contract figures are kept open.

deployments_procurement.summary: Drishti is a commercial multi-sensor EO satellite launched on rideshare; GalaxEye markets fused optical+SAR data rather than selling the spacecraft.
